title: HoHo Wien (Vienna timber high-rise): fire-protection framework and measures, as described in a 2021 diploma thesis
jurisdiction: Austria (Vienna project; OIB guidelines cited). Secondary analysis by a thesis; not the project's own fire report. Comparative only, not Alberta.
code_edition: OIB-330.2-012/19 table cited in the thesis annex (Anhang 5); thesis dated 2021-12-15

facts.text: Diploma thesis 'Brandschutzrechtliche Rahmenbedingungen holzbasierter Gebäude in Österreich', dated 15.12.2021 (author per repository file name).
HoHo Wien (Seestadt Aspern) is described as the tallest timber high-rise in Vienna, completed in 2019: 24 above-ground and two underground storeys, 84 m high, gross floor area about 25,000 m².
Structure: a reinforced-concrete core with attached timber elements (cross-laminated wall panels, glued-laminated timber columns, timber-concrete composite floor elements and precast edge beams).
The precast edge beam at the perimeter is described as an additional fire break that separates combustible wall and floor components.

The authority scrutinised the wall-to-floor connection. Fire tests on a 1:1 mock-up at the MA 39 test institute were needed to show no fire-through at the bearing point leading to structural failure. The thesis reports the test as successful, and reports an oversized (hot-design) section and a char layer slowing burn-through.
The thesis notes that planned timber-building guidelines (TRVB 110 F in 2009, and a later one) were not realised.

limitations: Secondary analysis by a diploma thesis. The project's fire concept and drawings are not in the attachment.
